## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input-group ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion @base-ui/react class-variance-authority ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — transitive registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — transitive registry dependency. - [@cadence/button](https://cadence.dev/r/button.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/input](https://cadence.dev/r/input.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/textarea](https://cadence.dev/r/textarea.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all 12 files in the target list, keeping `input-group/index.tsx`, `button/index.tsx`, `input/index.tsx`, `textarea/index.tsx` and the shared `lib/` files in the listed relative tree. Input Group imports Button, Input and Textarea even when a composition does not render every part. Its Button dependency needs the motion and provider helpers; those files are required imports, while wrapping the application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. No additional item-specific CSS is required beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities. The frame, addons, text and controls add no authored motion in full, reduced or none mode. `InputGroupButton` composes Button's press feedback: it scales only in full mode and drops that scale in reduced and none. Focus and invalid colour/ring changes are state feedback, not motion. Usage and the top preview also use [Kbd](/components/kbd). Install it when keeping the shortcut hint: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd ``` For manual installation, copy `files[].content` from the [Kbd payload](https://cadence.dev/r/kbd.json) to `@components/cadence/kbd/index.tsx`, reusing the `lib/cn.ts` already listed above. Kbd adds no npm dependencies beyond the shared helpers. It displays a shortcut hint; registering a keyboard shortcut belongs to the application. Usage, “A button in the frame” and the top preview also use `lucide-react` for their search/clear icons. Install it when keeping those icons; Input Group's recursive component dependencies do not require an icon package: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` Keep the source files' existing `"use client"` directives. In Next.js App Router, a Server Component can compose the client parts in Usage and Alignments with serializable props. Keep the existing client boundaries in “A button in the frame”, “A textarea with a footer”, Invalid and the preview; their hooks and event handlers stay there. Calling the exported `inputGroupAddonVariants` or `inputGroupButtonVariants` functions also belongs in a client module. Use `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea` for the control and give it an accessible name; addon text is not a label. Clicking an addon focuses its sibling input, unless the click is on a button or the caller prevents it; this convenience does not focus a textarea. Buttons keep their native focus and activation. The caller owns values, clearing, character limits, submission, error messages and `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`. Input Group renders that state and performs no validation; no validation package or schema setup is needed. ## Usage ```tsx import { SearchIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput } from "@/components/cadence/input-group"; import { Kbd } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function SearchField() { return ( ⌘K ); } ``` ## Alignments `align` places an addon before or after the control, inline or on its own block row. Editing this field does not silently clear an application error. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId } from "react"; import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput, InputGroupText } from "@/components/cadence/input-group"; export function InvalidEmail() { const id = useId(); return (

This email address is unavailable.

); } ``` ## When to use - A field with a fixed prefix or suffix: a currency symbol, `https://`, a unit, a domain. - A control that needs one inline action: search with a shortcut hint, a chooser with a clear button, an invite field with a submit button. - A textarea with a footer — a character count, a send button — where the footer must look attached to the field. ## When not to use - A bare text field. Use `input`; the group would only re-create its border. - A whole toolbar of actions. Use `button-group` beside the field, or a `form` layout: four buttons inside one field is a cramped target. - A label. Use `field` and `FieldLabel`; an addon is not an accessible name. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `InputGroup` | native div props | The frame; `role="group"`, focus and invalid state via `:has()`. | | `InputGroupAddon` | `align`, native div | `inline-start \| inline-end \| block-start \| block-end`, `data-align`. | | `InputGroupButton` | `size`, `variant`, `type`| `xs \| sm \| icon-xs \| icon-sm`; ghost by default. | | `InputGroupText` | native span props | Muted text or an icon; not a label. | | `InputGroupInput` | `input` props | Control with the frame's chrome removed; `data-slot="input-group-control"`. | | `InputGroupTextarea` | `textarea` props | Same, for multi-line. | The frame watches `[data-slot=input-group-control]` for `:focus-visible` and `[aria-invalid=true]`, which is why the control can be borderless and the group still shows the ring. `InputGroupButton` preserves Button state callbacks for `className` and `style`, with caller classes last. The input and textarea wrappers keep their native props. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). The frame never animates. `transition-[color,box-shadow]` covers the focus ring and the invalid border — state feedback that takes no space and does not run on mount. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - The addon text is not a name. Give the control an `aria-label`, or put a `FieldLabel` around the group through `field`. - `role="group"` on the frame and on each addon groups the pieces for assistive tech; add `aria-label` to the frame only if the group needs a name of its own. - The addon focuses the input on click — a convenience for pointer users. Keyboard users tab straight into the control, which is already the shortest path. - Buttons inside the frame keep their own names. An icon-only clear button needs `aria-label="Clear"`. - `aria-invalid` must be on the control, not on the frame; the frame reacts to it. ## Validation and data ownership P11: the group shows invalid state, it never decides it. | `InputGroup` does | You do | | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Draws the destructive border when a control is invalid | Deciding what is invalid | | Moves focus to the input when the addon is clicked | Wiring `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` | | Renders the buttons you give it | Submit, retry, error mapping | There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `resolver` prop, and no validation library is imported. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired. ## Responsiveness and performance The group fills its parent and permits shrinking. Block-start/end addons use column layout; inline addons share the input row. The caller owns long addon labels, button wrapping and narrow-screen composition. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Composed controls retain their own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Never wrap `input` in this group to "add a border"; the input already has one. - Put state on `InputGroupInput` (`aria-invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly`) — the frame is chrome, and it inherits the appearance. - Use `InputGroupButton`, not `Button`, inside the frame: the sizes are on the addon scale, and the addon's click handler recognises it as a button.
